decision.explanation: The projection is (a·b)/(b·b) times b. Since a·b=7−16+3=−6 and b·b=49+4+1=54, the projection is (−1/9)(7,−2,1)=⟨−7/9,2/9,−1/9⟩.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 7+8\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1}{{7}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{6}{54}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{7}{9},\frac{2}{9},-\frac{1}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components
content.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
content.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 7+8\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1}{{7}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{6}{54}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}⟨7,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{7}{9},\frac{2}{9},-\frac{1}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
